faq_heading: Price Reduced Homes for Sale in Surrey: your questions answered

faq.q: How much below asking are homes selling for in Surrey?
faq.a: SnapStats puts October 2026 at 96% of list price for Surrey detached homes (4% below) and 95% for condos and townhomes (5% below).

faq.q: Is Surrey a buyer's market or a seller's market?
faq.a: By the SnapStats reading, October 2026 was a buyer's market for detached homes (11% sales ratio) and a buyer's market for condos and townhomes (10%). The scale runs from a buyer's market under 12%, through balanced at 12% to 20%, to a seller's market above 20%.

faq.q: How long do Surrey homes take to sell?
faq.a: The typical Surrey detached home took 44 days to sell in October 2026, and a condo or townhome 28 days.

faq.q: Which price range has the most unsold detached homes in Surrey?
faq.a: $1,250,001 to $1,500,000, with 287 detached homes for sale and 29 sold in October 2026.

blocks.text: This search lists Surrey homes where the asking price has dropped by at least 1%, pulled live from the MLS®. Land and income properties are left out; houses, townhomes and condos are all included. The size of a price drop only makes sense next to the prices homes are actually closing at. In October 2026 a typical Surrey detached home sold for $1,248,000, took 44 days and closed at 96% of its list price, with 1033 detached homes for sale and 113 sold in the month.
What a price drop means in Surrey right now

Detached homes in Surrey have been selling about 4% under list price, and condos and townhomes about 5% under. On the detached side the sales ratio was 11%, which SnapStats reads as a buyer's market. For condos and townhomes it was 10%, also a buyer's market. A reduction of a few percent generally moves a home to where buyers have been paying, whereas a deeper one tells you the first price missed, and it is fair to ask by how much.

Supply is the other half. At October's pace the 1033 detached listings would take 9.1 months to sell, and the 1434 condo and townhome listings 9.8 months. Against October 2025, detached listings are 11% fewer and detached sales 22% more, which is the backdrop for how many price changes you will see.
Surrey detached homes by area: where buyers have room

Where stock is building up faster than it sells, sellers tend to reduce first. In October that was Queen Mary Park (66 listings, 3% sales ratio), Bolivar Heights (71 listings, 4% sales ratio), Whalley (81 listings, 5% sales ratio). The fastest-moving area was Cedar Hills, at a 27% ratio on 14 sales, so cuts there tend to be small or short-lived.

blocks.text: Price ranges with the most unsold Surrey detached homes

The busiest price range for listings was $1,250,001 to $1,500,000, with 287 homes for sale and 29 sold. The slowest of the well-stocked ranges were $2,250,001 to $2,500,000 (61 for sale, 2 sold); $2,500,001 to $2,750,000 (27 for sale, 1 sold); $2,000,001 to $2,250,000 (45 for sale, 2 sold). Buyers in those ranges have the most reason to expect room on price.
